comment: Determinism AND trust anchor for install_llama_prebuilt.py / install_whisper_prebuilt.py. release_tag pins the exact published release each installer installs by default, so one .dmg lands the same runtime on any day; without it both installers resolved 'newest published release' at install time and drifted. checksum_index_sha256 is ENFORCED at install time (prebuilt_core.verify_pinned_checksum_index): before an archive is trusted, the release's checksum_index_asset is fetched and its raw bytes must hash to the value below, giving the chain reviewed-in-tree-digest -> checksum index -> per-archive sha256 -> archive on disk. Verifying archives against an index served by the same release over the same TLS channel only proves the release is self-consistent; this digest is the one link the release host cannot forge. Enforcement applies ONLY to the release named here: an env-overridden tag, a --published-repo other than repo, UNSLOTH_PREBUILT_ALLOW_LATEST=1 or UNSLOTH_PREBUILT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 all mean no in-tree digest applies, and verification is skipped rather than failed. To bump: pick the new release tag per component, RE-RECORD checksum_index_sha256 (curl -sL the checksum_index_asset from that release | sha256sum) -- a bump that forgets this now fails the install closed rather than installing unverified -- update pinned_at_utc, and confirm the two components stay paired: whisper's manifest carries paired_llama_tag, which must equal llama_cpp.release_tag. Env overrides still win (UNSLOTH_LLAMA_RELEASE_TAG / UNSLOTH_WHISPER_RELEASE_TAG); UNSLOTH_PREBUILT_ALLOW_LATEST=1 restores the old track-latest behaviour; UNSLOTH_PREBUILT_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 installs without checking this digest.
